questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Unfair treatment of shorter people
The tallest people who have ever lived in history
How to become taller
Why women earn less than men
questions.why: The topic is heightism, a kind of discrimination against shorter people.

questions.q: How do Neil and Catherine feel about their own height?
options: Both wish they were much shorter
Catherine is unhappy with her height, but Neil is happy with his
Both are fine, though Neil wouldn't mind being taller
Neither of them has thought about it
questions.why: Catherine says she's alright with her height; Neil says the same, but wouldn't mind being slightly taller.

questions.q: Why does Catherine say the book title 'Shortchanged' is clever?
options: Because the author is very tall
Because the book is very short
Because the book is about getting the wrong change in shops
It's a pun about short people being treated unfairly
questions.why: She says in the context of discrimination against people who aren't tall, it's 'a really good pun'.

questions.q: What has Tanya S Osensky noticed about tall people?
options: Many of them wish they were shorter
None of them wish they were shorter
They don't like talking about height
They often say they are shorter than they are
questions.why: She says 'I have not met anybody who said they would wish they were shorter.'

questions.q: What do people often do when asked how tall they are?
options: Refuse to answer
Give their exact height
Say they are shorter than they really are
Say they are taller than they really are
questions.why: She says people tend to embellish their height, saying they are taller than they are.

questions.q: According to research, which of these is true for shorter people?
options: They are less likely to get jobs and promotions
They are more likely to be promoted
They work longer hours
They are better at their jobs
questions.why: Neil says research shows shorter people are less likely to get jobs, be promoted or earn as much.

questions.q: How much extra per inch of height do men earn, according to one set of data?
options: Over $2000
questions.why: She says the premium for height is over $2000 per inch for men and $1000 for women.

questions.q: What does Tanya S Osensky say happens to this pay difference over time?
options: It disappears
It stays the same from the first job until the last one
It grows into a big part of career earnings
It only affects women
questions.why: She says the disparity grows significantly, becoming 'a huge chunk of someone's paycheck'.
